explanation: This is the sharpest link in the third movement and it runs backwards through thirty years. The Allies lost ninety-seven per cent of Asian rubber production when Japan took Malaya at the beginning of 1942 — and the production was Asian in the first place because seeds taken out of Brazil in 1876 had been planted in British colonies and had undercut the Amazon by 1912. The collapse of the Brazilian monopoly is what put the world’s rubber inside Japan’s reach, and that is what sent the United States back to the Amazon to buy what it had stopped buying.
